text:
sam: heads-up — saw a big flurry of new GPU nodes in us-west1 this morning around 09:03. cost spike + some tails on inference P99. looks like HPA lat-metric triggered replica surge and CA brought up new nodepool members too aggressively.

mira: ugh. which metric? latency or queue depth?

sam: our HPA is wired to external metric `inference_queue_latency_ms` (prom-adapter). graph: https://grafana.redwood/aui/board/123?panel=queue_latency

deploy-bot: Autoscaler event: scaleUp: need 8 nodes (gpu-mem-high) — reason: 42/48 pods unschedulable (needs nvidia.com/gpu=1).

jordan: are pods requesting GPUs directly or scheduling onto GPU nodepool via nodeSelector? we have two GPU nodepools: gpu-burst (preemptible) and gpu-reserved (on-demand). CA might be preferring burst if expander is `least-waste` -> ends up creating many small patched nodes.

sam: pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and tolerations/taints are set. They prefer `gpu-reserved` via nodeAffinity but affinity is `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` so CA can still put them on new nodes.

kai: I suspect HPA reacts to transient latency spikes (10s of seconds) and scales replicas before any warm-cache or batching kicks in. That combined with CA's autoscale groups (scale-up cooldown 0s) causes nodepool churn.

mira: we saw similar last month. fix was smoothing in the external metric server (prom-adapter) + use `behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds` in the HPA. also consider `horizontal-pod-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/behavior` annotations.

jordan: concrete suggestions:
- switch HPA to use `averageValue` on queue-length (requests in queue) rather than latency. queue-length is less noisy.
- add `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120` for scaleUp + `policies` with `type: Percent` limit to cap spike.

sam: +1. also CA config: set `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--balance-similar-node-groups` flags? we currently have `expander: least-waste`, maybe change to `expander: random` or use `priority` with nodegroup-priority annotation so reserved pool is used first.

kai: CA supports `nodegroup.kubernetes.io/priority` annotation? We use cluster-autoscaler v1.26 — it supports `--expander=priority` with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority` on node groups. Setting gpu-reserved higher priority should prefer it.

mira: caution: priority expander will still create nodes if high-priority group is saturated. For cost control, mark gpu-burst as lower priority and also add `--max-node-provision-time=15m` so preemptible startup that's slow won't block.

sam: another angle: prevent HPA from scaling past X replicas when no spare GPUs exist — use a `KEDA` scaled object with `scaleTargetRef` and `minReplicaCount/maxReplicaCount` to enforce a soft cap and better backoff. anyone experimented with KEDA + CA for GPUs?

jordan: we've tried KEDA on CPU-backed services. For GPUs, KEDA's scaler for Prometheus is fine. It supports `cooldownPeriod` and `pollingInterval`. Could replace HPA or run alongside with `behavior` to avoid double-scaling.

kai: also look at VPA interactions: I noticed a couple pods got restarted after VPA applied `resourcePolicy` changes and that triggered rescheduling which created more pending pods and CA scaled. We should disable VPA eviction for GPU workloads or set `updateMode: "Off"` and surface recommendations only.

sam: yep — will change VPA updateMode to `Off` for `inference-*` namespaces.

mira: steps I'm going to take:
1) Patch HPA to add `behavior` with `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120` and `policies` limiting scaleUp to 50% per 60s.
2) Change HPA metric to `queue_length` average.
3) Smooth prom-adapter with `window=30s` to reduce spikes.

sam: I'll add nodegroup priorities: annotate `gpu-reserved` with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority=100` and `gpu-burst` with `5`. Also increase `scale-down-unneeded-time` to 12m.

jordan: i'll prototype a small KEDA scaler for canary workload in staging to validate behavior.

kai: ops item: disable VPA `updateMode` for inference namespaces (set to Off) and add a monitor alert if pods restart during rollout.

mira: small kubectl snippets for the HPA patch:
```bash
kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -n inference --type merge -p '\n{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":120,"policies":[{"type":"Percent","value":50,"periodSeconds":60}]}}}}'\n
```

sam: CA annotation snippet:
```bash
kubectl annotate nodegroup gpu-reserved cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority=100 --overwrite
kubectl annotate nodegroup gpu-burst cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority=5 --overwrite
```

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: hpa-patch will run at 10:30 if approved.

mira: approved :thumbsup:

sam: i'll follow up after today’s peak. if this fixes it we should add a runbook: "gpu-surge -> check HPA metric window, verify CA nodegroup priorities, disable VPA evictions".

jordan: logging note: add `pending_pod_count` metric to infra dashboard so we can see CA pressure before node creation.

kai: and add alert rule: `pending_pod_count > 10 for 3m` -> notify #eng-oncall.

sam: thanks all — i'll do the VPA + annotation changes now and post updates.

mira: thanks, will schedule KEDA test in staging this afternoon.

sam: update 10:45 — patched HPA in staging with stabilization window, queue metric switched; no node churn on the small synthetic spike. rolling to prod in 15.

mira: nice! :party-parrot:

sam: prod deployed 11:05 — initial heat: p99 looks stable, CA created 2 nodes instead of 7. keeping an eye on cost dashboard.

jordan: great. add follow-up to retro for deeper analysis of metric choice and CA expander behavior.

kai: closing for now, reopen if we see >$5k/day spike.

sam: closing thread.
